newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope decries "endless" tragedy in central Africa.
newsitem.headline: Pope decries "endless" tragedy in central Africa.

text.p: Pope John Paul urged the world community on Wednesday to help end central Africa's "interminable tragedy" and warned that those mistreating their brothers and sisters there would be accountable before God.
"I sincerely hope the international community will do all in its power to bring help effectively to the catastrophe which is raging," the Pope told pilgrims in St Peter's Square.

"With unspeakable sorrow, I am following events in north-eastern Zaire, where ferocious fighting and looting has forced thousands of Rwandan and Burundian refugees, especially the elderly, women and children, into an aimless flight."
The conflict has already forced half a million Hutu refugees to flee camps in eastern Zaire.
The Tutsi-dominated governments in Rwanda and Burundi see the Hutu refugees, thousands of whom are former soldiers of the ousted Rwandan government, as a potential threat.

The 76-year-old Pope, who has visited all the countries involved in the current central African crisis, spoke as reports of artillery exchange between Zaire and Rwanda fuelled fears of a widening Central African conflict.
"It is an interminable tragedy...It is agonising to see how human beings, who are sons of God and brothers of ours, are being treated," the Polish Pope said.

Zaire has warned Rwanda it would fight to defend its territory and vast mineral wealth against its small eastern neighbour. It accuses the Rwandan army of supporting Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels who are fighting Zaire.
Rwanda's military strongman has threatened to retaliate against the Zairean shelling which he said had killed many people in the Rwandan border town of Cyangugu.
"It is anguishing to see how human beings who are children of God and who are our brothers are being treated. The Lord will call everyone to account," he said.
"I pray for guns to be silenced, for hatred and ethnic rivalries to be placated and that an end to be put to the shameful manhunt that is taking the place of negotiations."
